en.title: The Witcher 4 Box Will Have 'Feelies' Even if Discs Disappear
en.summary: CD Projekt Red confirms The Witcher 4 will offer a physical edition with collectible 'feelies,' even as disc-based releases face an uncertain future. Fans can expect a tangible package, but the traditional game disc is likely out.
en.body:
The long-awaited **The Witcher 4** is on the horizon, with CD Projekt Red targeting a 2028 release. This ambitious timeline, however, brings a significant question to the forefront: will the game be available on a physical disc? With major console manufacturers like Sony and Microsoft reportedly phasing out disc support around the same time, the prospect of a traditional disc release for Geralt's next adventure seems increasingly unlikely.

CD Projekt Red's joint CEO, Michał Nowakowski, addressed this directly, stating that the studio has "no influence" over the hardware manufacturers' decisions regarding disc production. "The discs for the first parties, including PlayStation, have to be manufactured in their own factories. So, if they stop manufacturing indeed by 2028, then yes [we won’t have a disc]," he explained. This pragmatic outlook acknowledges the evolving industry landscape, where digital distribution is becoming the norm.

## A Tangible Experience for Fans

Despite the potential absence of a physical disc, CD Projekt Red remains committed to providing players with a tangible connection to the game. Nowakowski emphasized the company's appreciation for physical collectibles, a sentiment shared by many within the studio. "We’re big fans of people having access to tangible collectible things. We’re nerds ourselves, and we like that. We always supported that," he stated. This passion translates into a promise for **The Witcher 4**: a physical edition that will include a special "box" filled with "feelies." These "feelies" are described as items that players will "be wanting to open up and enjoy," suggesting a curated collection of in-game or franchise-related memorabilia designed to enhance the collector's experience.

## What This Means for The Continent's Faithful

For the devoted fanbase of **The Witcher** saga, this announcement offers a welcome compromise. While the convenience and ubiquity of digital downloads are undeniable, many players, particularly those who grew up with earlier generations of gaming, cherish the ritual of unboxing a new game and displaying their physical collections. CD Projekt Red's acknowledgment of this desire, and their commitment to delivering a premium physical product even without a disc, shows a deep understanding of their audience. This approach ensures that the *spirit* of a physical release—the anticipation, the discovery, and the tangible mementos—will still be present for **The Witcher 4**, even as the medium itself shifts.

## The Road Ahead

**The Witcher 4** is set to kick off a new trilogy, with subsequent titles planned for release within a six-year window, potentially concluding by 2034. Alongside this new saga, CD Projekt Red is also working on a **The Witcher 3 Remastered** and an expansion titled *Songs of the Past*. Details regarding the specific contents of **The Witcher 4**'s physical "feelies" box have not yet been announced.

content_raw: CD Projekt Red recently confirmed that the long-awaited RPG The Witcher 4 is targeting a release in 2028 , and that timing has led many to wonder if the Polish developer will offer the game on a disc. After all, Sony is ending support for physical PlayStation discs in 2028 and Microsoft is expected to ditch discs, too. CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski told The Game Business that the studio has "no influence" on what companies like Sony and Microsoft choose to do with regards to supporting discs. "The discs for the first parties, including PlayStation, have to be manufactured in their own factories. So, if they stop manufacturing indeed by 2028, then yes [we won’t have a disc]," he said. At the same time, Nowakowski stressed that CD Projekt Red is a company that is highly fond of giving people "access to tangible collectible things." Given that, the executive teased that The Witcher 4 will, "for sure," have some kind of "box." "We’re nerds ourselves, and we like that. We always supported that. So, whatever is the case, we’re going to be for sure having a box. We’re going to have a box that’s going to have some feelies in it," he said. "Something you’re going to be wanting to open up and enjoy. But we have no influence actually on what’s the case here." The Witcher 4 kicks off a new trilogy of The Witcher games, spanning The Witcher 4, 5, and 6. These games are planned to all be released within a six-year window, so the entire trilogy could be here by the end of 2034. In addition to these three new The Witcher games, CD Projekt is working on The Witcher 3 Remastered and a new expansion for the game called Songs of the Past . Additionally, the team is developing Cyberpunk 2 , a The Witcher multiplayer game , and a game made in partnership with Scopely .
